T2.name: Family multi-class (5-way)
T2.description: Classify 5 known families in Subset A.

T3.name: Concept drift (pre- vs post-2024-09)
T3.description: Discriminate pre-2024-09 from post-2024-09 samples (time_bucket classification) on the standard split, measuring the temporal signal carried by the static features.

T4.name: Open-set detection (Subset A known vs. B novel families)
T4.description: Open-set / novel-family detection. Fit a multi-class classifier on the Subset A known families (splits.json key T4_open_set: known_train=3826, known_val=546), then at test time score the held-out known_test (987 Subset-A samples) against the test-window Subset B novel-family partition (267 samples; n_unknown=267) using maximum-softmax-probability and free-energy OOD scores. Subset A and Subset B share no AVClass family, so B functions as out-of-distribution. splits.json key T4_open_set also records the full 1359-sample Subset B unknown_pool; the reference baseline scores the 267 test-window members for split-consistency with the other tasks, and scoring the full 1359-sample pool changes AUROC by under 0.001.

T5.name: Hybrid static + dynamic fusion
T5.description: Late fusion of static (LightGBM on parquet) and dynamic (TF-IDF on CAPE Reduced) predictions.

T6.name: Few-shot family (N=5, K in {5,10})
T6.description: Episodic few-shot evaluation over 8 ultra-rare families in Subset C.

T7.name: Non-UPX packer detection
T7.description: Binary detection of samples carrying a non-UPX packer signature (489 positives) vs samples with no packer signature (9,430 negatives). Labels derive from the EMBER2024 'packer' field, NOT from subset membership; the 81 UPX-only samples are excluded so the negative class is clean. Subset E3 is a curated 191-sample slice of the positives and is not itself the task label.
T7.target_rule: positive iff packer list contains any entry != 'upx'; negative iff packer list is empty; exclude UPX-only samples

T8.name: Exploit / CVE detection
T8.description: Binary detection of exploit-bearing samples (111 positives, exploit field non-empty) vs samples with no exploit (9,889 negatives). Labels derive from the EMBER2024 'exploit' field, NOT from subset membership; Subset E1 is a curated 109-sample slice of the positives and is not itself the task label.
T8.target_rule: positive iff exploit list is non-empty; negative otherwise

T9.name: APT group-tag prediction (6-way)
T9.description: Single-label prediction over the 177 samples in Subset E2 into one of 6 APT-group buckets in subset_class (collapsed from 14 capa-derived group tags). These are weak, capa-derived labels for group-tag prediction, NOT validated threat-actor attribution. Note: a 'group' tag appears on 217 samples corpus-wide; this task deliberately uses the 177-sample curated Subset E2 (the dedicated APT rare-gem subset). The 40 group-tagged samples outside E2 carry incidental group tags under a different primary subset assignment and are excluded to keep a clean, closed-set APT task (this is a curation choice, not a one-vs-rest contamination). Under the primary timestamp split the 32-sample E2 test partition contains no apt_molerats instances (19 train incl. validation / 0 test) and a single apt_knotweed instance, so the reported 6-way macro-F1 averages over one structurally unscorable class and should be read as a conservative floor for this exploratory weak-label task, not a calibrated attribution score.

T10.name: Capa capability multi-label
T10.description: Predict the 579 distinct capa capabilities (caps_list column).

T11.name: MITRE ATT&CK TTP multi-label
T11.description: Predict the 96 distinct MITRE ATT&CK techniques (ttps_list column).

T12.name: MBC behaviour multi-label
T12.description: Predict the 186 distinct MBC behaviours (mbc_list column).

T13.name: Per-architecture detector (Win32/Win64/.NET)
T13.description: Train per-architecture binary detector; report AUC per file_type.

T14.name: Capability count regression
T14.description: Regress total capa+TTP+MBC capability count per sample.

T15.name: Evasive-malware challenge (OOD detection, 96 samples)
T15.description: Detection of the 96 initially-undetected (evasive) malicious samples in the challenge split, scored against the test-split benign samples as negatives. The challenge split is 96 malicious / 0 benign, so it is evaluated as out-of-distribution / evasive detection, NOT as standalone binary accuracy.
T15.subset_filter: positives: dyn_split == 'challenge'; negatives: dyn_split == 'test' and label == 0
